subject: LLM telemetry: PII segregation, egress path & subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Devon Reed <devon.reed@atlas-ai.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas AI Security <security@atlas-ai.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: telemetry PIi mapping, egress & subprocessor evidence for DPA annex

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this — Atlas is doing a DPA annex review tied to our data residency and telemetry controls. We have a couple of focused asks before our security committee signs off: 

1) Does Redwood collect or persist any PII in LLM telemetry (inference logs, prompts, completions) by default? If so, where and for how long?
2) Can you provide a simple diagram or description of the egress path for telemetry and model payloads (which services are involved, any third-party subprocessors, and where data leaves customer VPCs)?
3) For any subprocessors involved in telemetry or observability (metrics, logs, tracing), can you share a short evidence list (SOC2 certs, region of processing, rough retention windows)?
4) Is there an off-the-shelf tokenization/pseudonymization step we can rely on for PII redaction upstream of any long-term storage?

We’d like a one-page summary + attachments (diagrams, classification matrix, attestation) by EOD Tuesday if possible. Appreciate any interim notes.

Cheers,
Devon
Devon Reed
Security Engineer, Atlas AI
devon.reed@atlas-ai.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry PIi mapping, egress & subprocessor evidence for DPA annex

Devon — thanks for the clear list. High-level answer up front: we do not persist raw customer prompts/completions as PII by default in our hosted offering; telemetry is split into (a) aggregated usage metrics and (b) short-lived inference traces used for debugging which are redacted/hashed unless a customer opts into extended diagnostics. Below are bullets and attachments; Priyom/Markus are cc’d for technical details and artifacts.

Summary (short):
- PII persistence: Not by default. We treat prompts/completions as customer data; only aggregated metrics (token counts, latency distributions) are stored permanently. Inference traces that may contain PII are retained for 7 days and are redacted using our token-redaction pipeline unless the customer explicitly enables extended storage for debugging (customer opt-in).
- Egress path: Customer request -> Redwood inference runtime (VPC endpoint) -> optional telemetry proxy -> metrics/logs to Datadog (EU/US regions configurable) and object store (S3) for transient traces. Diagram attached.
- Subprocessors: Datadog (metrics), Amazon S3 (transient trace storage), GCP Pub/Sub (optional routing). See Prioym’s note for SOC2/region details.
- Tokenization/redaction: We apply a two-stage approach: local heuristics + regex-based classifiers, then a hashing/pseudonymization step before long-term storage. This is documented in the attached classification matrix.

Attachments included: pii-classification-matrix-20261003.csv, llm-telemetry-dataflow-v2.png

Next steps: Priyom can provide the subprocessor evidence and retention windows; Markus can confirm encryption/KMS custody. If Atlas needs a formal attestation we can produce a one-page KMS attestation doc.

Let me know if the attached diagram is sufficient for your committee or you want a simplified one-pager.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: telemetry PIi mapping, egress & subprocessor evidence for DPA annex

Hi Devon / Jasmine — quick technical follow-up with concrete subprocessors and retention windows: 

- Metrics: Datadog (processed metrics, no raw prompts) — region configurable; default US. Retention policy: 90 days for detailed metrics, 13 months for aggregated roll-ups. Datadog is SOC2 Type II (vendor attestation available).
- Transient traces: Amazon S3 in customer-chosen region (encrypted at rest with our CMK). Retention: default 7 days, configurable per-customer via Console.
- Tracing/Logs: Optional push to GCP Pub/Sub or AWS Kinesis for customers that route telemetry into their own systems. We do not hand raw inference payloads to third parties except S3 transient storage.

Data handling notes: 
- Any trace that matches PII patterns is marked and pseudonymized locally before it's written to S3. The pseudonymization uses HMAC with our service key (per-customer salt). Raw values are never stored unless the customer explicitly enables an extended debug session and signs a data retention addendum.
- Key custody: Redwood holds the CMK in our KMS; customers can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) in Dedicated and Private deployments — note that BYOK changes the recovery/rotation model.

Evidence we can provide (attached or on request): vendor SOC2 summaries for Datadog and AWS, export logs showing region/processing, and a brief CSV mapping (attached by Jasmine).

If Atlas needs the vendor SOC2 PDFs we can upload them to the Drive link Jasmine provided.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Architect, Inference Platform
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Devon Reed <devon.reed@atlas-ai.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry PIi mapping, egress & subprocessor evidence for DPA annex

Devon — quick clarity on KMS and pseudonymization implementation: 

- Encryption/KMS: All transient traces written to S3 are encrypted using a CMK (AWS KMS) that Redwood manages by default. For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) — in those configs customer owns key lifecycle and revocation.
- Pseudonymization: We don’t rely on simple hashing alone. We use an HMAC with per-customer salt + rotating pepper stored in KMS; this ensures pseudonymous IDs cannot be trivially reversed. The HMAC output is what is stored in traces/longer retention objects.
- Access controls: Only a small number of backend service accounts (tagged with role:inference-debug) can access unredacted traces and only from a restricted bastion with session recording. Access is audited and retained in our audit log (30 days by default; extended retention available as an add-on).

If Atlas needs an explicit statement about whether raw prompts are ever transmitted to third-party analytics vendors: short answer is no — we route derived metrics and pseudonymized traces only.

Happy to do a short call if the committee wants to walk the diagram.

-Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
